Presentation
SIS-LPEBL KT is a private independent primary bilingual (English/French) school welcoming pupils aged 3 to 10 years old. Pupils are taught English and French on a strict schedule parity basis.
SIS-LPEBL KT teaches both curricula : the National Curriculum of England and the Education Nationale French program.
SIS-LPEBL KT favours small number year groups where we can nurture each child's learning and well-being.
SIS-LPEBL KT implements a project based teaching, organises a lot of school outings and is committed to enabling each and every one of our pupils to be happy "letting their intelligence have fun".

pageCache.text:
OUR ETHOS
The principal aim of our school is to offer an ambitious and inclusive bilingual curriculum in a happy, caring and intellectually stimulating environment. We aim for every pupil to feel a valued member of the school community and to have a sense of being personally nurtured. We recognise our responsibility to safeguard and promote the welfare of all our pupils by protecting them from physical, sexual or emotional abuse, neglect and bullying.
Caring - Effort - Creation
Let’s investigate, dream, create : let our intelligence have fun!
Discover our curriculum
Admission and school fees
Discover our school in pictures
How a day at school unfolds

ABOUT US
Lady Anne Henderson-Stewart founded "Le Jardin d'Enfants Bilingue" in 1975 and "La Petite Ecole Française" in 1983 in London and welcomed and taught children from very different international backgrounds. This school was part of the French schools offer in London and of the AEFE network.
Then in 1995, based on her London experience, Lady Anne Henderson-Stewart created "La Petite Ecole Bilingue" in Paris.
In 2007, Lady Anne Henderson-Stewart sold "La Petite Ecole Française", in order to focus only on her fully bilingual project in Paris. "La Petite Ecole Bilingue de Londres" was born in 2010, first of the bilingual campuses in London, in Oxford Gardens. In September 2012 was created the Kentish Town branch of "La Petite Ecole Bilingue de Londres" which provides for pupils aged 3 to 10 year old. 2017 saw the creation of a fourth school in Bordeaux (France).
Today, "Stewart International School - La Petite Ecole Bilingue" is a group of 4 campuses located in London, Paris and Bordeaux.

A LITTLE BIT OF HISTORY...
SIS – LPEBL KT is housed in Saint Martin’s church former vicarage in Gospel Oak since September 2012.
Built in 1904, this previous religious building is Grade 1 listed. It was sold to a first private landlord by the parish some 40 years ago.
Saint Martin’s church has been welcoming its parishioners since it was built in 1865. Mother Carol Barrett Ford also hosts our school’s events with always such a warm welcome and open mind.

CURRICULUM
SIS-LPEBL KT teaches both curricula : the National Curriculum of England and the Education Nationale French program.
Programme Education Nationale Française
National Curriculum in England (Sept 2013)
Two pedagogic coordinators are responsible for building bridges between the two curricula and ensuring that teaching plans are logical and appropriate.
Our bilingual curriculum can be viewed at school upon request.
How a day at school unfolds
MOST COMMON QUESTIONS
History, Geography and Science curriculum
Other particularities at SIS-LPEBL KT
How do we teach reading in both languages ?
We teach our pupils how to read in English first in Reception year (Moyenne Section) thanks to small groups "phonics" sessions. The main objectives of this year are for the children to understand the mechanisms of the blending technique, and to know how to decipher and write simple words and also to start to learn the "tricky words". By the end of Year 1, pupils will have learned how to read and write according to the English Curriculum progression.
The discovery of French phonèmes and graphèmes starts later in Grande Section (Year 1) to be completed in CP (Year 2) with a more systematic teaching of reading with the syllabic method.
Whatever the language, we actually only learn how to read once in a lifetime. But we benefit here from the natural transfer of the reading skills acquired in English towards the reading of French which is usually acquired faster in our environment. Learning how to read happens then alternatively and not simultaneously which enables each pupil to integrate each language's various sounds at their own pace and avoid any confusion.
How do we provide both curricula entirely when we actually teach each language half week ? What happens especially with the science, history and geography ?
Teaching two curricula does not mean repeating each learning objective in both languages.
An important part of our pedagogic work has been to gather the common learning objectives in both curricula and at the same time, list all the specific abilities. It was then possible to draw a clear and efficient teaching plan per year group.
For instance in mathematics, expected objectives are identical even though teaching strategies may often vary. Pointing this out enables us to optimise our teaching time for the benefit of all the topics.
Our cross curricular projects are then very useful as we can gather several learning objectives in one teaching sequence. While cross curricular teaching keep the pupils very focused and curious, it also leads the group to tackle a greater number of skills at the same time.
To sum up, we would say that we especially focus on the learning objectives regarding mathematics and language and that we definitely put history, geography and science at the heart of our teaching plans.
How do you deal with the arrival of new pupils, especially in older primary year groups ?
We welcome bilingual or English beginner pupils in our older primary year groups. A good level in French is nonetheless required in those age groups.
Whenever complete English beginner pupils join us from Year 2 (CP), a teaching assistant is added to the teacher whenever needed. Pupils can then be despatched in smaller groups during some specific sessions focused on basic vocabulary ; beginners can also be helped during lessons by the assistant offering extra-help on a one to one basis.
Our low number year group are very helpful and efficient here: 20 pupils per age group.
We encourage parents of these beginner pupils to try to provide support at home eg from a nanny, or by enrolling the child in some after-school clubs.
Any other particularities at SIS – LPEBL KT ?
We organise many school outings : learning outside the school broadens the pupils’ horizon and gives a more palpable meaning to the various projects we implement.
Finally, our school’s cosy environment with low number year groups enables our pupils to feel listened to, to be able to be different and to develop a certain pride of belonging to this small community.

JOB OFFERS
KS1 and / or KS2 English Teacher
KS1 and / or KS2 English Teacher Assistant
Un(e) professeur(e) des écoles (Cycles 2 et/ou 3)
KS1 and/or KS2 English Teacher - International School in Central London
Well established international bilingual (French & English) school in Central London is currently looking for an enthusiastic KS1 and/or KS2 English teacher from September 2024.
- a caring and dedicated teacher who will create strong bonds with his/her pupils.
- applicants with a good knowledge of KS1 and/ or KS2 curricula.
- enthusiastic, inspiring and creative teacher with a passion for his/ her profession.
- someone with a strong team spirit who will be able to work in tandem with the French form teacher.
- someone with strong organisational skills.
- committed to high standards of presentation and organisation in his/her work and behaviour in his/her classroom. Expects similar high standards from his/ her pupils.
- Small class sizes.
- Opportunities to take on additional responsibilities within the school and to teach across several year groups.
- Very strong community ethos, warm welcoming environment and supportive colleagues and parents.
- Rich and stimulating bilingual curriculum.
- Lovely and inspiring children from across the world who speak 2, 3 and sometimes 4 languages. Curious and eager to learn.
KS1 and/or KS2 English Teacher Assistant - International School in Central London
Well established international bilingual (French & English) school in Central London is currently looking for an enthusiastic English speaking Teacher Assistant from September 2024.
- a caring and dedicated teacher assistant who will create strong bonds with his/her pupils.
- applicants with a Level 2 equivalent.
- someone with a strong team spirit who will be able to work in tandem with the class teacher.
- someone with strong organisational skills.
- committed to high standards of presentation and organisation.
- Small class sizes.
- Very strong community ethos, warm welcoming environment and supportive colleagues and parents.
- Rich and stimulating bilingual curriculum.
- Lovely and inspiring children from across the world who speak 2, 3 and sometimes 4 languages. Curious and eager to learn.
Cycle 2 French Teacher - International Bilingual School in Central London
Well established international bilingual (French & English) school in Central London is currently looking for an enthusiastic Cycle 2 French Teacher from September 2024.
- a caring and dedicated teacher who will create strong bonds with his/her pupils.
- applicants with a good knowledge of Cycle 1 and/or 2 French curriculum.
- enthusiastic, inspiring and creative teacher with a passion for his/ her profession.
- someone with a strong team spirit who will be able to work in tandem with the English form teacher.
- someone with strong organisational skills.
- committed to high standards of presentation and organisation in his/her work and behaviour in his/her classroom. Expects similar high standards from his/ her pupils.
- Small class sizes.
- Opportunities to take on additional responsibilities within the school and to teach across several year groups.
- Very strong community ethos, warm welcoming environment and supportive colleagues and parents.
- Rich and stimulating bilingual curriculum.
- Lovely and inspiring children from across the world who speak 2, 3 and sometimes 4 languages. Curious and eager to learn.
The school follows a French academic school calendar (17 weeks school holidays; 1st week: 1st week of September; last week: 1st week of July).
The school is committed to safeguarding children and young people. All post holders are subject to a satisfactory Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check.
If you are interested please fill in this form and send a CV and a cover letter by email to office@lpebl-kt.com .​​

HOW A DAY AT SCHOOL UNFOLDS
8.25 am : school doors open
8.40 am : school doors close
8.45 am : lessons start
4.00 pm : end of lessons (12.00pm on Wednesdays)
There are two lunch services at midday :
11.30 am : Pupils from Nursery until Year 1 have lunch (1st service).
12.00 am : Pupils from Year 2 until Year 6 have lunch (2nd service).
After their lunch Nursery pupils have a nap time when the other pupils enjoy a quiet moment and then a long playtime (45 min).
Lessons start again at 1.15 pm for all year groups.

School assembly (twice month)

pageCache.pageTitle: La Petite Ecole Bilingue de Londres KT - Admission
pageCache.text:
ADMISSION
SIS - La Petite Ecole Bilingue de Londres - Kentish Town is a bilingual private independent primary school welcoming pupils from various cultural backgrounds from the age of 3.
Pre-application at SIS – LPEBL KT is free and can be done at any time of the year. Parents wishing to pre-apply for their child need to complete the online form available below.
Link to the online pre-application form
2- School place offer
School place offers are made according to our Admission Policy following the pre-application process.
Parents receive a School Place offer email which details the various required formalities to be completed by parents in order for the offer to be approved.
The School Place offer is valid for 10 days.
All the required documentation has to be sent back by email to : office@lpebl-kt.com.
Registration is complete once all the formalities detailed below have been fulfilled within the deadline.
read the “Terms and Conditions”, the “Financial Policy” and any document attached to the email.
send a copy of the child's valid passport
send copies of both parents' valid passports
in the case of divorce or separation: send a copy of the divorce or separation court order or a letter signed by both parties regarding child custody arrangements if no court order has been handed down
copies of the child's last three school reports (when available)
pay the £1,200 first application fee
pay a £1,000 advance on first term fees.
NB : in case of cancellation, these payments are not refundable.
